data.title: Discover the Magic of Uzbekistan, 8 days (Private)
data.description: Discover the magic of Uzbekistan - where vibrant culture, rich history, and breathtaking architecture come together to create an unforgettable journey. From ancient Silk Road cities to lively local bazaars, every moment is filled with beauty, flavor, and adventure. Experience the heart of Central Asia like never before.

events.description: Arrival in Tashkent. The guide and driver will warmly welcome you at the outdoor waiting area of Tashkent International Airport. After your arrival, enjoy a short rest before setting off to discover a city where ancient heritage meets modern elegance. Hotel check-in is available from 2:00 PM.

Exploring the magnificent Khast Imam Complex, one of the city’s most important spiritual and historical landmarks
Experiencing the lively atmosphere of Chorsu Bazaar, a colorful market filled with local flavors, spices, and traditional crafts
Lunch time (not included)

Riding the iconic Tashkent Metro, famous for its beautifully designed stations, including Kosmonavtlar, Alisher Navoi, Paxtakor, and Mustaqillik Maydoni
Enjoying a relaxing walk through Sayilgoh Street, the lively heart of the city, where you will admire landmarks such as Amir Temur Square, the State Museum of the Temurids, the first hotel in Uzbekistan, and the Palace of Congresses from the outside.
Return to the hotel. Rest and overnight

Meet the driver at the hotel entrance.
Transfer to the railway station.

Transfer to Samarkand by a high-speed train.
* please note that the departure time is not guaranteed and can be changed

Visiting the magnificent Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum (14th–15th centuries), the final resting place of the great Amir Temur (Tamerlane). Built during the Timurid era, this architectural masterpiece continues to captivate visitors from around the world with its elegance, grandeur, and stunning blue dome.
Exploring the world-famous Registan Square (15th–17th centuries), the true heart of ancient Samarkand, surrounded by the majestic Ulugbek, Tillakori, and Sherdor madrasahs — some of the finest examples of Islamic architecture in the world.
Lunch time (not included)

Discovering the mystical beauty of the Shah-i-Zinda Necropolis, a sacred complex of beautifully decorated mausoleums known for its dazzling mosaics and spiritual significance.
Admiring the impressive Bibi-Khanym Mosque (14th–15th centuries), once one of the grandest mosques in the Islamic world and a symbol of Amir Temur’s powerful empire.
Enjoying free time at Siyob Bazaar, the city’s most famous local market, where you can experience authentic Uzbek culture, taste traditional sweets and fresh fruits, and shop for unique souvenirs and spices.
Return to the hotel. Rest and overnight
Meet the guide and proceed to explore Samarkand.

Explore the peaceful Imam al-Bukhari Memorial Complex, dedicated to the world-famous Islamic scholar Imam al-Bukhari, one of the most respected figures in Islamic history. This spiritual and beautifully designed complex is an important pilgrimage site and a place of reflection and cultural heritage.
Lunch time (not included)

Experience the artistry of traditional craftsmanship at the Meros Paper Mill, where ancient paper-making techniques have been preserved for generations. Watch skilled artisans transform mulberry bark into exquisite handmade paper using methods dating back to the Silk Road period, and discover one of Samarkand’s most unique cultural traditions.
VVVisit the remarkable Ulugh Beg Observatory (15th century), one of the greatest astronomical observatories of the medieval world. Built by the renowned Timurid ruler and astronomer Ulugh Beg, this fascinating site offers a glimpse into the advanced scientific achievements of the Silk Road era. Discover the ancient instruments and innovative techniques once used to map the stars and explore the mysteries of the universe centuries ahead of their time.
Return to the hotel. Rest and overnight

Today, enjoy a scenic journey through the beautiful landscapes of Uzbekistan as we travel from Samarkand to the historic city of Bukhara, one of the most important cultural gems of the Silk Road. The journey covers approximately 450 km and takes around 5 hours. Upon arrival, check-in at the hotel and rest.
Lunch time (not included)

Discover the charming Lyabi-Hauz Complex, one of the most atmospheric corners of Bukhara, surrounded by historic madrasahs, traditional teahouses, and a peaceful pond at the heart of the old city.
Explore the ancient Covered Oriental Markets (16th–17th centuries), where the spirit of the Silk Road still lives on through colorful handicrafts, local souvenirs, spices, textiles, and traditional artisan workshops.
Return to the hotel. Rest and overnight

This morning, continue discovering the timeless beauty of Bukhara with visits to some of its most iconic historical treasures:
Ismail Samani Mausoleum (9th–10th centuries) — one of the oldest and finest masterpieces of Islamic architecture in Central Asia.
Chashma-Ayub Mausoleum (12th–16th centuries) — a sacred site linked to fascinating legends and ancient traditions.
Bolo Haouz Mosque (18th–20th centuries) — admired for its elegant wooden columns and beautiful architecture.
Ulugh Beg Madrasa (15th century) — one of the oldest madrasahs in Central Asia, built by the famous astronomer and ruler Ulugh Beg, reflecting the region’s rich educational and cultural heritage.
Lunch time (not included)
Ark of Bukhara (5th–20th centuries) — the majestic ancient fortress that once served as the residence of Bukhara’s rulers for centuries.
Return to the hotel. Rest and overnight

Today, we travel through the scenic landscapes of Uzbekistan to the legendary city of Khiva. Known for its perfectly preserved old town, Itchan Kala — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — Khiva feels like an open-air museum of the Silk Road.
The journey from Bukhara covers about 450 km (around 6 hours), with a memorable lunch stop in the desert along the way.
Upon arrival, we check into the hotel and enjoy a well-deserved rest after the journey, preparing to explore the historic wonders of Khiva.
Meet the guide at the hotel and proceed to explore Khiva.

Sightseeing in Khiva includes:
Muhammad Amin Khan Madrasa and the iconic Kalta Minor Minaret — one of the city’s most recognizable landmarks with its striking turquoise facade.
Kunya-Ark Fortress — the ancient citadel that once served as the residence of Khiva’s rulers, offering stunning views over the old city.
Muhammad Rahim Khan Madrasa — a beautiful 19th-century educational center reflecting Khiva’s cultural and scholarly heritage.
Juma Mosque (Khiva) — a unique wooden-column mosque known for its peaceful atmosphere and remarkable architectural design.
Tash Khovli Palace and the Khan’s Harem — a beautifully decorated royal residence showcasing traditional Khorezm architecture. (Approx. visit time: 40–50 minutes)
Ollaquli Khan Caravanserai — a historic trading hub that once welcomed Silk Road merchants. (Approx. visit time: 20–30 minutes)
Islam Khodja Complex — including the elegant madrasah and the tallest minaret in Khiva, offering stunning views of the old city. (Approx. visit time: 40–60 minutes)
Pahlavon Mahmud Mausoleum — a sacred and beautifully tiled complex dedicated to the city’s patron saint. (Approx. visit time: 30–40 minutes)
Local Bazaar — a vibrant market where you can experience authentic Khivan life, shop for souvenirs, and enjoy local crafts. (Approx. visit time: 30–45 minutes)
Free afternoon.

Transfer to the Urgench airport 3 hours before your departure time.
Departure from Urgench.
End of the tour services.

terms.serviceNote:
As travel organizers in Uzbekistan, we work with European agencies and travelers with a clear understanding of their expectations and operating standards. Flexibility, adaptability and service quality are central values for TourLink.

Our approach to hotels
We select hotels according to comfort, aesthetics, atmosphere and charm, with a preference for boutique properties. Our partner hotels are reviewed regularly, and we prioritize locations close to city centers or quiet areas suitable for rest in larger cities. Transfers in large cities are organized and included in our services.

Our approach to restaurants
Restaurants are selected according to the local character of each stop. We favor traditional establishments and coordinate menus with restaurant teams so travelers can discover the flavors of each region.

Our transport service
We provide vehicles with professional drivers and maintain regular quality control. Private guides are selected carefully and evaluated frequently to keep service standards high.

Classic and extended travel
Classic tours cover the main highlights of Uzbekistan. For longer stays, we can propose additional routes and personalized suggestions after our exchange.
